text: A secretary died with nine million dollars. Even her husband may never have known.
And she got it from her boss, without stealing a cent.
Sylvia Bloom worked at one New York law firm for sixty-seven years.
Secretary's salary. Took the subway to work, into her nineties.
But every time her boss bought a stock, she bought the same one. Just a lot less of it.
No tips. No tricks. She copied, and she waited. For decades.
When she died in twenty sixteen, at ninety-six, her family found accounts at three brokerages and eleven banks.
And she gave it away. Six point two million became scholarships for New York students in need.
She never earned a big salary. What made her rich wasn't how much she made. It was how long she waited.
